editorial:
Imagine spending over four decades in a tiny cell for a crime you did not commit. That is exactly what happens to Iwao Hakamada, a former pro boxer who finds himself trapped in a legal nightmare. You get to see the heartbreaking reality of a man who is pushed to his breaking point by a system that refuses to listen to the truth. The movie feels heavy and serious, but it keeps you hooked because you just want to see this man get the justice he deserves. It is not an action movie, but the emotional battle is just as intense as any boxing match.

What really makes this film work is the raw acting. You can feel the pain and confusion in every scene. The pacing is a bit slow at times, which might bore some people, but it helps you feel how long and dull those prison years actually were. If you love true crime stories that make you think about fairness, you need to see this. It is definitely worth the time if you want a story that stays with you long after the credits roll.
endingExplained: The movie ends by showing the long, painful road toward Hakamada's release. You see how new evidence and determined lawyers finally prove that the police lied and faked the evidence against him. He is eventually freed from prison and found innocent, but the ending is bittersweet. While he is finally out, the film makes it clear that he can never get back the forty years of his life that were stolen from him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about justice and legal battles.
